heroHeadline: 24 Days to Kickoff — Neymar Confirmed by Ancelotti in Brazil's Final 26-Man Squad; Iran Departs for Antalya Camp With Zero US Visas; Zurich Summit Tomorrow (May 20)
heroSubtitle: Carlo Ancelotti announced Brazil's final 26-man World Cup squad at the Museum of Tomorrow in Rio de Janeiro on May 18, with Neymar Jr. (34) confirmed despite his dramatic late form question — the Santos forward was accidentally substituted off in tears during Santos' 3-0 loss to Coritiba the day before, sparking a wave of public sympathy that may have contributed to Ancelotti's decision to include him. Key absences stand: Rodrygo (ACL), Eder Militão (hamstring), and Estevao Willian (Grade-4 hamstring). Vinicius Junior, Endrick, Matheus Cunha, Bruno Guimaraes, and Gabriel Magalhaes headline the confirmed inclusions. Meanwhile, Iran's national team departed Tehran for a training camp in Antalya, Turkey on May 18 — with not a single US entry visa issued to any Iranian player or coaching staff. The formal FIFA-Infantino-Taj summit in Zurich is now two days away (May 20), the last diplomatic channel before the June 1 final squad submission deadline and 24 days before the June 11 opener at Estadio Azteca. Austria, Croatia, Curaçao, and DR Congo also announced final squads on May 18; Iran announced its roster on May 17, omitting Sardar Azmoun. Upcoming: Germany (May 21, Nagelsmann), England (May 22, Tuchel at Wembley — Ben White out MCL), and USMNT (May 26, live NYC event on FOX — Pulisic, McKennie, Adams, Balogun expected). FIFA publishes all 48 squads June 2. Tubi/FOX World Cup Hub live with 24/7 programming and simulcast of the opening ceremony plus two matches.
